junction.name: 7 Avenue & West 42 Street, New York City

claims.text: 7 Avenue & West 42 Street had 81 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 36 pedestrians injured, 28 cyclists injured and 0 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.5 million a year.
31% of crashes here involved a two-wheeler, against 16% at the city's priority junctions.
17% of crashes here involved a taxi or for-hire car, against 6% at the city's priority junctions.
15% of crashes here had a cyclist hurt, against 7% at the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading south and it happened in the night (7 pm to 6 am) in 15% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 6% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading south and a two-wheeler was involved in 13% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 4% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Leading Pedestrian Interval would avoid about 0.9 crashes a year (CMF 9918, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the city's own past installs passed the causal gate), worth $312,000 a year.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 2.4 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $832,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for 7 Avenue, West 42 Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 3, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 5.
A request letter to the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 3, New York City Council; Manhattan Community Board 5
Subject: Request for safety study at 7 Avenue & West 42 Street

Dear colleagues at NYC DOT,

We are writing to ask NYC DOT to carry out a safety study at 7 Avenue & West 42 Street.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 177 crashes, including 81 injury crashes. 36 pedestrians and 28 cyclists were injured, and no one was killed. The yearly cost of the harm, in the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), is $5.5 million. This junction is a city priority location. In this period there is a recorded safety project: Broadway, 41-42 BIKE BLVD in 2026.

We ask you to assess, for the roads you are responsible for, the following:

For 7 Avenue and West 42 Street, a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green), which is expected to prevent 0.9 pedestrian injury crashes per year, avoiding $312,000 in harm per year, and which pays for itself if it costs less than $2.2 million. Where the city installed it at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain.

For 7 Avenue and West 42 Street, longer yellow signal times, which is expected to prevent 4.4 injury crashes per year, avoiding $1,509,000 in harm per year, and which pays for itself if it costs less than $10.6 million, subject to a site check for an entry on yellow or red.

Thank you for your consideration.

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]

- NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (corridors); NYC DOT Street Improvement Projects (intersections); NYC Vision Zero View, Enhanced Crossings (6ax4-q5k4); NYC Vision Zero View, Leading Pedestrian Interval Signals; NYC Vision Zero View, Signal Timing/25 MPH Retiming; NYC Vision Zero View, Speed Humps (jknp-skuy); NYC Vision Zero View, Turn Traffic Calming; NYC Vision Zero priority corridors; NYC Vision Zero priority intersections
- FHWA CMF Clearinghouse, CMF 9918 (a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green))

- Road owners: the registry's road-inventory layer (see the engineer report's receipts)
